partner_result_applied.application: Applied the partner weighted local Edgeworth expansion for normalized uniform banks to the exact two-bank density integral p_Qm(0)=int int g_m(b)g_m(c) 1_{c^2<=|b|}/(2|b|) db dc, obtaining p_Qm(0)=C_null-I_null/(20m)+O(m^-2). The partner's separate exact rotated witness supplies C_*>=3sqrt(2).

new_results: For arbitrary cap-one X independent of B,C iid N(0,1/12), Q=2XB+C^2 has a bounded continuous density and the zero-density functional is uniquely maximized a.e. by X uniform on [-1/2,1/2].
The exact extremal constant C_null obeys C_null<3sqrt(2) analytically via the pointwise Laplace-transform inequality int_{-1/2}^{1/2} exp(-s x^2) dx < (1+s/6)^(-1/2).
Diagnostic quadrature gives C_null=3.62066702814959078157..., leaving a 0.6219736589696944... gap below 3sqrt(2).
Exact finite source-valid rotated family with one null heavy row and two diffuse m-banks has nonzero spectrum exactly {1,1,-1} and form Q_m=2X_0 B_m+C_m^2.
Partner Edgeworth theorem applied to its exact zero-density integral gives p_Qm(0)=C_null-I_null/(20m)+O(m^-2), with explicit finite I_null and diagnostic I_null=11.6540810558260528....
scope_warning: This excludes only the one-heavy isotropic/null-row plus two Gaussianizing diffuse-bank sharp-witness architecture. It does not prove the full conjecture, prove C_*=3sqrt(2), or prove global centered-interval extremality for arbitrary rotated forms.
continuity: Proved for the Gaussian-completion theorem and for the stated finite witness family under the bank regularity supplied by the partner theorem; full-target continuity remains open.
unresolved_implication: Whether a witness with at least two mesoscopic/heavy directions, several non-collinear shared rows, or a genuinely multiscale three-bank geometry can exceed 3sqrt(2); independently the full universal upper bound remains open.
next_step: Change witness mechanism to two mesoscopic/heavy shared directions or a multiscale non-bank construction while preserving exact cap-one product provenance and the three-large-eigenvalue condition.
